solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drive forward the French backs

parts.note: a prop is a forward in a rugby scrum

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the French article is read in reverse

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A rugby report: the French back line drives the play forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive forward' reads as one definition and 'backs' as rugby players; 'forward' is a rugby position and 'backs' means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel something is to push or drive it onward.

clue.text: Factor sure to be involved with extremes of haemolysis

indicators.note: being involved means the letters are tangled together and rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A medical note: some factor is certainly bound up with the breakdown of red blood cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of haemolysis' gives H and S, mixed with SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhesus factor is a blood-group antigen, so 'Factor' alone is a fair shorthand for it.

clue.text: Where one might go to pot after the rack's been used

definitions.text: Where one might go to pot after the rack's been used

parts.words: Where one might go to pot after the rack's been used
parts.note: in snooker or pool the balls are set up in a triangular rack and then potted on a green baize surface

explanation.surface: Seems to describe someone who goes to ruin after torture on the rack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to pot' and 'rack' suggest decline and torture; both are cue-sport terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls are racked and then potted on the green-topped playing surface in a game of pool.

clue.text: Theme sounds superficial: insufficient reason to take action

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: light, as in light reading, means superficial

indicators.note: insufficient means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: An argument that a shallow theme gives no good reason to act.
explanation.walkthrough: LEIT is said like LIGHT; MOTIVE loses its last letter to give MOTIV.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical or literary theme associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: Writer is hard to follow, like Burns

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, the novelist
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A complaint that a writer is difficult to follow, much like the poet Burns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' only confirms the order of the pieces. Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was a Scot, so something like him is of Scotland.

clue.text: Disturb cat endlessly returning to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch means to hold something inside
returning means the shortened word is read backwards
endlessly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A cat keeps coming back to grab a fish, upsetting everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the cat word to PUS, and 'returning' turns that into SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake up is to unsettle or disturb something, often a group or organisation.

clue.text: Tipsy cake of sorts is given poor marks

parts.note: to cake is to coat thickly, and to oil is a kind of coating
E and D are low exam grades

explanation.surface: A boozy cake, like a trifle, gets bad reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cake' is a verb here (coat), not a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, so it means tipsy.

clue.text: Coach house to evict daughter — about time!

indicators.note: to evict is to throw out, so this letter is removed
about signals the replacement letter going round into the gap

parts.note: the Tudors were an English royal house

explanation.surface: Someone finally throwing a daughter out of the coach house.
explanation.walkthrough: In TUDOR the D is thrown out and T takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor coaches a pupil, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Plan to dispense with Christmas broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast signals that the phrase is spoken out loud

parts.note: to shed is to dispense with, and Yule is Christmas

explanation.surface: A proposal to scrap the Christmas programmes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: SHED YULE spoken in British English, with a soft 'sch', matches SCHEDULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetabled plan of events.

clue.text: Unity's repelled by appeal artist holds for young lady

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: unity is one, so Unity's gives ONE'S

indicators.note: holds means one piece contains the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
it is a word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A tangled sentence about a painter whose charm deters unity, with a girl in it.
explanation.walkthrough: ONES backwards gives SENO; RA holds IT for RITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Senorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman or girl.

clue.text: Plant desire in Juliet's heart

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the heart of a word is its centre letters

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Romeo plants a longing in Juliet's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the noun definition; the heart of a six-letter name is its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, or lychee, is a Chinese fruit tree.

clue.text: Standard practice for hack to receive special award

indicators.note: to receive is to take something in

parts.note: to hack is to cut
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Is it normal for a journalist to get a special prize?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist but means CUT. The OM is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is an established usage or habit, the normal way things are done.

clue.text: Place fabulously loaded with gold

indicators.note: fabulously suggests something made up, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A legendary place simply laden with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulously' also hints at the legend itself; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the mythical South American city of gold sought by explorers.

clue.text: Plump, owing to lack of exercise (apparently)

parts.note: O, zero, stands for nothing at all
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone is fat, seemingly because they never work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' is the verb (plump for), not the adjective it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is to choose it, the same as to opt.

clue.text: Could it be used to pelt bacteria indirectly?

definitions.text: Could it be used to pelt bacteria indirectly?

indicators.note: indirectly means in a roundabout way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about firing something at germs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PELT BACTERIA gives the answer, and the whole clue describes radiation bombarding microbes.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta particles are high-energy electrons, a form of radiation that can sterilise by killing microbes.

clue.text: One returning to employment is right to accept a tenner in review

indicators.note: a container that accepts a guest lets it in, so the other piece goes within these letters
a review re-examines and reworks, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A returning worker is right to take ten pounds when looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in review' makes the solver rework A TENNER, and a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-entrant is someone who comes back in, such as a person rejoining the workforce.

clue.text: Suffering from debt: realising means of liquidation?

definitions.meaning: liquidation is also what happens to bankrupt firms

explanation.surface: A firm in debt sees liquidation coming.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into IN SOLVENT: a solvent is what turns solids to liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolvent company cannot meet its debts and is often wound up by liquidators.

clue.text: Perpetual bankrupt at last in prison under pressure from international group

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another sits below it

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
broke means bankrupt

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A permanently bankrupt prisoner is leaned on by the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'under pressure from' puts the bankrupt part below the international group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken continues without interruption, so it is continuous or perpetual.

clue.text: They may probe between the eyes

parts.note: inter- is the Latin prefix meaning between
viewers are eyes, the things that view

explanation.surface: Something might poke someone right between the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between the eyes' sounds like a spot on the face, but is read as a Latin prefix plus a word for onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Interviewers ask probing questions of the people they question.

clue.text: Fantastic flyer for Sound of Music?

indicators.note: sound of signals that the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: rock is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A nod to the film The Sound of Music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of Music' looks like the film title but means 'what rock sounds like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian tales, so a creature of fantasy that flies.

clue.text: Editor and setter take over top third of workplace building

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: taking off the top third removes the first two of six letters

parts.note: an office is a workplace

explanation.surface: Editor and setter seize the top floors of an office block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take over' suggests seizing control; it means remove the top third, OF, from OFFICE, leaving FICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure.

clue.text: Animal working pit railway's gone missing

indicators.note: gone missing means these letters are taken away

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An animal at the pit, and the railway line has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLIERY loses RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Vegetable gives brother colic when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

explanation.surface: A vegetable upsets a brother's stomach while he is out on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: COLIC with its last C cycled to the front gives CCOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Pursuit ends in trollop and detective being taken for a ride

indicators.note: being taken for a ride means riding inside, so these letters go in

parts.note: a car is a ride

indicators.note: ends picks out the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A chase ends with a loose woman and a detective being conned.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of trollop and detective, P and E, go inside CAR. 'Pursuit ends' looks like one phrase; Pursuit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is an escapade or activity, a pursuit undertaken for fun or gain.

clue.text: Mother-to-be likes restricting symbols in texts

indicators.note: restricting means holding within limits, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman's likes are curbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger or division-sign marks used in printed texts for footnotes or doubtful passages.

clue.text: Grease left Travolta exhausted initially, then dispirited

indicators.note: initially says this piece comes first, before the letter for left
exhausted means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: low means downhearted

explanation.surface: The film Grease left John Travolta worn out at first, then gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grease' looks like the Travolta film but is the definition. TRAVOLTA emptied leaves TA, placed before L.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap, a kind of grease.

clue.text: Crack jokes about Portugal's capital

indicators.note: about means going round another piece
to crack is to break apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Telling jokes about Lisbon, Portugal's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: JOKES rearranged around P. 'Portugal's capital' wants to mean Lisbon or P; the capital is Skopje, North Macedonia's.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the capital city of North Macedonia.

clue.text: She's one to make a sound tax-free investment as an outsider

indicators.note: an outsider stays on the outside, so these letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: an ISA is a UK Individual Savings Account, which is tax-free
an gives the letter A
a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: A woman who invests tax-free while not being one of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; with 'an' it forms the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's name, so she is an example of a female person.

clue.text: Excite rebellious Frenchman to confront soldier's base

indicators.note: rebellious suggests turning against, so the name is reversed

parts.note: René is a French man's name
GI is an American soldier, so soldier's gives GI'S
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A French rebel squares up to a soldier's camp.
explanation.walkthrough: RENE reversed is ENER; 'base' means E, the mathematical constant, not a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill with energy, to stimulate or excite.

clue.text: Exclude women from social site for a laugh

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so this letter goes

parts.note: Twitter is a social media site

explanation.surface: Banning women from a social network, just for a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: TWITTER without W.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short nervous or suppressed laugh.
